paragraphs.title: The Commandments and Entering the Land

easy.question: What did the Lord command the Israelites to be taught?
answers: The commandments, statutes, and judgments
The names of the kings
Ways of conducting trade
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord commanded Moses to teach Israel the commandments, statutes, and judgments.

easy.question: Who is mentioned as needing to keep the Lord’s commandments?
answers: Only the elders
You, your son, and your son’s son
Only the priests
easy.explanation: The verse emphasizes keeping the commandments across several generations: you, your son, and your son’s son.

easy.question: How is the land that the Lord gives Israel described?
answers: A land of high mountains
A land of great rivers
A land flowing with milk and honey
easy.explanation: The land is described as a land flowing with milk and honey.

medium.question: What is one purpose of keeping the Lord’s statutes and commandments?
answers: That their days may be prolonged
So they will not need to learn
So they will leave the land
medium.explanation: The passage says that keeping the commandments would help prolong their days.

medium.question: What order of ideas appears in these verses?
answers: Many children, leaving the land, and teaching
Teaching the commandments, keeping them, and receiving blessing in the land
Receiving the land, forgetting the commandments, and hearing
medium.explanation: First the commandments are taught, then they are kept and practiced, resulting in well-being and increase in the land.

medium.question: In the phrase “the land whither ye go to possess it,” what does “possess it” mean?
answers: To leave it
To learn about it
To receive it and live in it
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to entering the land in order to receive it and settle in it.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the mention of “you, and your son, and your son’s son”?
answers: Keeping the commandments is meant to continue from generation to generation
Only sons are allowed to study the Torah
The commandments are valid for only one day
challenge.explanation: Mentioning three generations emphasizes the continuing teaching and observance of the commandments.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “Hear therefore… and observe to do it” teach?
answers: It is enough merely to hear the command
Hearing should lead to keeping and doing
One should act without knowing the command
challenge.explanation: The verse connects hearing with observing and doing, so understanding the command is not enough without putting it into practice.

challenge.question: What is the connection between keeping the commandments and “that it may be well with thee, and that ye may increase mightily”?
answers: Blessing will come only to the leaders
Increase depends on conquering other lands
Obedience is connected with blessing, well-being, and increase in the promised land
challenge.explanation: The passage presents keeping the commandments as part of the way to experience blessing and increase in the land promised to the ancestors.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the mention of “you, and your son, and your son’s son”?
answers: Keeping the commandments is meant to continue from generation to generation
Only sons are allowed to study the Torah
The commandments are valid for only one day
questions.explanation: Mentioning three generations emphasizes the continuing teaching and observance of the commandments.

questions.question: What does the phrase “Hear therefore… and observe to do it” teach?
answers: It is enough merely to hear the command
Hearing should lead to keeping and doing
One should act without knowing the command
questions.explanation: The verse connects hearing with observing and doing, so understanding the command is not enough without putting it into practice.

questions.question: What is the connection between keeping the commandments and “that it may be well with thee, and that ye may increase mightily”?
answers: Blessing will come only to the leaders
Increase depends on conquering other lands
Obedience is connected with blessing, well-being, and increase in the promised land
questions.explanation: The passage presents keeping the commandments as part of the way to experience blessing and increase in the land promised to the ancestors.

paragraphs.title: Hear, O Israel, and Love the Lord

easy.question: To whom is the call “Hear, O Israel” addressed?
answers: The people of Israel
The kings of Egypt
The angels of heaven
easy.explanation: The verse directly addresses the people of Israel.

easy.question: What does verse 4 say about the Lord?
answers: He is far from Israel
He is one
He is invisible
easy.explanation: The verse declares, “The Lord our God is one Lord.”

easy.question: How does the verse command Israel to love the Lord?
answers: Only in thought
Only through outward actions
With all the heart, soul, and might
easy.explanation: The verse calls for complete love: with all the heart, soul, and might.

medium.question: What is the relationship between the two verses?
answers: First Israel declares who the Lord is, and then is commanded to love Him
First the Exodus is described, and then the giving of the Torah
The second verse cancels the first
medium.explanation: Verse 4 declares that the Lord is one, and verse 5 continues with the command to love Him completely.

medium.question: In the phrase “with all thy might,” what does “might” refer to?
answers: Every place where you are
All your strength and everything you have
Everything you hear
medium.explanation: Together with heart and soul, “might” refers to dedicating all one’s strength and resources to the Lord.

medium.question: What idea is emphasized by the repeated phrase “with all” in verse 5?
answers: Love for the Lord should be complete, not partial
One must choose only one of the three things
The command applies only to strong people
medium.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that love includes the heart, soul, and every ability and resource.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the order “with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might”?
answers: The command concerns emotion only, not action
The command moves from the body to thought alone
The command includes the inner person and all his resources
challenge.explanation: Heart and soul refer to the inner person, while “might” extends the command to all one’s strength and possessions.

challenge.question: What is significant about the verse saying “the Lord our God” rather than only “the Lord”?
answers: It emphasizes the Lord’s relationship with Israel
It teaches that Israel has several gods
It says that the Lord belongs only to one place
challenge.explanation: “Our God” expresses Israel’s relationship and belonging to the Lord.

challenge.question: Which wording emphasizes that the command is addressed to all Israel together?
answers: The singular word “thy soul”
The address “Hear, O Israel”
The word “one” at the end of the verse
challenge.explanation: “Hear, O Israel” addresses Israel as a people and presents the declaration and command as a communal matter.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the order “with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might”?
answers: The command concerns emotion only, not action
The command moves from the body to thought alone
The command includes the inner person and all his resources
questions.explanation: Heart and soul refer to the inner person, while “might” extends the command to all one’s strength and possessions.

questions.question: What is significant about the verse saying “the Lord our God” rather than only “the Lord”?
answers: It emphasizes the Lord’s relationship with Israel
It teaches that Israel has several gods
It says that the Lord belongs only to one place
questions.explanation: “Our God” expresses Israel’s relationship and belonging to the Lord.

questions.question: Which wording emphasizes that the command is addressed to all Israel together?
answers: The singular word “thy soul”
The address “Hear, O Israel”
The word “one” at the end of the verse
questions.explanation: “Hear, O Israel” addresses Israel as a people and presents the declaration and command as a communal matter.

paragraphs.title: Passing the Torah on at All Times

easy.question: Whom are the Israelites commanded to teach and instruct?
answers: Their children
Their neighbors
The kings
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children.”

easy.question: Where are the words to be written?
answers: On clothing
On the doorposts of the house and on the gates
On the vessels of the sanctuary
easy.explanation: The passage says to write them on the doorposts of the house and on the gates.

easy.question: What are the Israelites to bind on their hand?
answers: The words as a sign
A mezuzah
A book
easy.explanation: The verse commands, “Thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thine hand.”

medium.question: In the phrase “Thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children,” what does “teach them diligently” mean?
answers: To teach and repeat them carefully
To hide them
To draw them
medium.explanation: The phrase describes carefully teaching and repeating the words so that the children know them well.

medium.question: Why does the Torah mention both sitting at home and walking along the way?
answers: To limit learning to the home
To show that the Torah should be discussed in different times and places
To teach that it may be discussed only on the road
medium.explanation: The passage includes the home, the road, lying down, and rising up, showing that the words should accompany a person throughout the day.

medium.question: What is the general order of actions in these verses?
answers: Writing, lying down, teaching, and rising
Binding, writing, speaking, and teaching
Receiving the words, teaching them to others, remembering them, and marking them
medium.explanation: The words are first to be in the heart, then taught and discussed, and finally marked on the hand, between the eyes, and on the doorposts.

challenge.question: Which list includes all the times mentioned for speaking about the words?
answers: At home, on the road, when lying down, and when rising
Only in the morning and in the synagogue
Only at home and at the city gate
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions sitting at home, walking along the way, lying down, and rising up.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from moving from “these words… shall be in thine heart” to binding, writing, and speaking?
answers: The words are intended only for private thought
Faith should be inward and also visible in actions and daily life
There is no need to remember the words after writing them
challenge.explanation: The verses begin with an inward attitude and continue with teaching, speaking, symbols, and writing, connecting inner faith with action.

challenge.question: Which phrase emphasizes that the command is not limited to one time of day?
answers: “This day”
“Thy house”
“When thou liest down, and when thou risest up”
challenge.explanation: Mentioning lying down and rising up points to the end and beginning of the day, emphasizing continual observance.

questions.question: Which list includes all the times mentioned for speaking about the words?
answers: At home, on the road, when lying down, and when rising
Only in the morning and in the synagogue
Only at home and at the city gate
questions.explanation: The passage mentions sitting at home, walking along the way, lying down, and rising up.

questions.question: What can be inferred from moving from “these words… shall be in thine heart” to binding, writing, and speaking?
answers: The words are intended only for private thought
Faith should be inward and also visible in actions and daily life
There is no need to remember the words after writing them
questions.explanation: The verses begin with an inward attitude and continue with teaching, speaking, symbols, and writing, connecting inner faith with action.

questions.question: Which phrase emphasizes that the command is not limited to one time of day?
answers: “This day”
“Thy house”
“When thou liest down, and when thou risest up”
questions.explanation: Mentioning lying down and rising up points to the end and beginning of the day, emphasizing continual observance.

paragraphs.title: Abundance and the Danger of Forgetting

easy.question: Who will bring the Israelites into the land?
answers: The Lord their God
The ancestors
The kings
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord their God will bring them into the land.

easy.question: What will the Israelites receive in the land that they did not build or prepare?
answers: Only tents
Cities, houses, wells, vineyards, and olive trees
Only pasturelands
easy.explanation: The verses describe cities, houses, wells, vineyards, and olive trees that the Israelites did not build or plant.

easy.question: What does the passage warn the Israelites not to do?
answers: Not to eat fruit
Not to build houses
Not to forget the Lord
easy.explanation: The passage warns, “Then beware lest thou forget the Lord.”

medium.question: Why does Moses warn Israel immediately after describing abundance in the land?
answers: Because abundance may cause them to forget the Lord
Because they are forbidden to enjoy the land
Because the land is not suitable for living
medium.explanation: After eating, becoming full, and enjoying great possessions, the people might forget who brought them out of Egypt.

medium.question: In the phrase “wells digged, which thou diggedst not,” what does “digged” describe?
answers: Covered with earth
Made by digging into the ground or rock
Filled with water
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to wells prepared by digging, though the Israelites did not dig them.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in the verses?
answers: The people forget, leave Egypt, and then receive houses
The people plant vineyards, build cities, and then leave Egypt
The Lord brings the people into the land, they enjoy abundance, and then they are warned not to forget
medium.explanation: The passage first describes entering the land and receiving prepared possessions, then becoming full, followed by the warning.

challenge.question: What is the main contrast between the description of the land and the memory of Egypt?
answers: In the land there is prepared abundance, while in Egypt the people were bondmen
In the land there are no houses, while Egypt had many houses
In the land the people work hard, while in Egypt they were free
challenge.explanation: The verses contrast abundance in the land with Egypt, where the people were enslaved.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the cities, houses, and vineyards were not built or planted by Israel?
answers: The land was completely empty
They received a blessing that was not the result of their work alone
They were not allowed to use what they received
challenge.explanation: The repeated statement that they did not build or plant these things emphasizes that they received them as a gift and should remember its source.

challenge.question: Which phrase strengthens the connection between the warning and the Exodus?
answers: The word “cities”
The mention of vineyards and olive trees
The phrase “which brought thee forth,” referring to the Lord
challenge.explanation: This phrase explicitly recalls that the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt, so He must not be forgotten during times of abundance.

questions.question: What is the main contrast between the description of the land and the memory of Egypt?
answers: In the land there is prepared abundance, while in Egypt the people were bondmen
In the land there are no houses, while Egypt had many houses
In the land the people work hard, while in Egypt they were free
questions.explanation: The verses contrast abundance in the land with Egypt, where the people were enslaved.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the cities, houses, and vineyards were not built or planted by Israel?
answers: The land was completely empty
They received a blessing that was not the result of their work alone
They were not allowed to use what they received
questions.explanation: The repeated statement that they did not build or plant these things emphasizes that they received them as a gift and should remember its source.

questions.question: Which phrase strengthens the connection between the warning and the Exodus?
answers: The word “cities”
The mention of vineyards and olive trees
The phrase “which brought thee forth,” referring to the Lord
questions.explanation: This phrase explicitly recalls that the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt, so He must not be forgotten during times of abundance.

easy.question: What does the passage command Israel to do toward the Lord their God?
answers: Fear Him and serve Him
Serve the gods of the nations
Avoid all worship
easy.explanation: The verse commands Israel to fear the Lord, serve Him, and swear by His name.

easy.question: Whom must Israel not follow?
answers: The priests
Other gods
The leaders of the people
easy.explanation: The passage explicitly says, “Ye shall not go after other gods.”

easy.question: What may happen if Israel serves other gods?
answers: The people will receive wealth
The nations will help them
The Lord’s anger will burn against them and destroy them from the earth
easy.explanation: The passage warns that serving other gods may bring the Lord’s anger and destruction.

medium.question: What order of actions appears in verse 13?
answers: Fear the Lord, serve Him, and swear by His name
Swear by His name, fear Him, and serve Him
Serve other gods and then swear by the Lord’s name
medium.explanation: The verse presents the order: fear the Lord, serve Him, and then swear by His name.

medium.question: In the phrase “the Lord thy God is a jealous God,” what does “jealous” mean here?
answers: A god who does not care about human actions
A God who requires exclusive loyalty and will not accept the worship of other gods
A god who never punishes
medium.explanation: In context, “jealous” describes the Lord’s demand for exclusive loyalty, immediately connected with the warning against other gods.

medium.question: How does verse 15 explain the prohibition in verse 14?
answers: Because the surrounding nations are stronger than Israel
Because other gods exist only in the wilderness
Because the Lord is among Israel and may become angry if they serve others
medium.explanation: Verse 15 explains that the Lord is a jealous God among His people, so serving other gods could provoke His anger.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “and serve him”?
answers: Worship of the Lord must be exclusive and not combined with worship of other gods
There is no need to fear the Lord
Any god may be worshiped depending on the place
challenge.explanation: The emphasis on serving Him connects with the prohibition against other gods and teaches exclusive loyalty to the Lord.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “among you” emphasize in verse 15?
answers: The Lord is only outside the land
The Lord is present among Israel, so their actions matter to Him
The Lord belongs only to the surrounding nations
challenge.explanation: “Among you” emphasizes the Lord’s presence within Israel and the people’s responsibility not to serve other gods.

challenge.question: Why does the passage mention the gods of the people “which are round about you”?
answers: To teach that all nations worship the Lord
To say that Israel may not live near other nations
To warn against the nearby influence of the surrounding nations’ practices
challenge.explanation: Mentioning the surrounding peoples highlights the nearby danger that their worship and practices could influence Israel.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “and serve him”?
answers: Worship of the Lord must be exclusive and not combined with worship of other gods
There is no need to fear the Lord
Any god may be worshiped depending on the place
questions.explanation: The emphasis on serving Him connects with the prohibition against other gods and teaches exclusive loyalty to the Lord.

questions.question: What does the phrase “among you” emphasize in verse 15?
answers: The Lord is only outside the land
The Lord is present among Israel, so their actions matter to Him
The Lord belongs only to the surrounding nations
questions.explanation: “Among you” emphasizes the Lord’s presence within Israel and the people’s responsibility not to serve other gods.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the gods of the people “which are round about you”?
answers: To teach that all nations worship the Lord
To say that Israel may not live near other nations
To warn against the nearby influence of the surrounding nations’ practices
questions.explanation: Mentioning the surrounding peoples highlights the nearby danger that their worship and practices could influence Israel.

paragraphs.title: Do Not Tempt the Lord; Do What Is Right

easy.question: Whom must Israel not tempt?
answers: The Lord their God
Their enemies
Their ancestors
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Ye shall not tempt the Lord your God.”

easy.question: What are the Israelites commanded to keep?
answers: Only the land
The Lord’s commandments, testimonies, and statutes
Only their enemies
easy.explanation: Verse 17 commands Israel to keep the Lord’s commandments, testimonies, and statutes.

easy.question: What will happen when Israel does what is right and good in the Lord’s sight?
answers: They will leave the land
They will stop keeping the commandments
It will be well with them, and they will possess the land
easy.explanation: The passage says that doing what is right and good will bring well-being and possession of the good land.

medium.question: Why does the Torah command Israel to do what is right and good in the Lord’s sight?
answers: So that it may be well with them and they may possess the land
So they will not need to keep the commandments
So they may tempt the Lord
medium.explanation: The passage connects doing what is right and good with well-being, possessing the land, and driving out enemies.

medium.question: In the phrase “to cast out all thine enemies,” what does “cast out” mean?
answers: To remember
To drive away and remove
To invite
medium.explanation: In the context of enemies, “cast out” means to drive them away or remove them.

medium.question: What order is described in these verses?
answers: Possessing the land, keeping commandments, and then doing good
Tempting the Lord, leaving the land, and then keeping commandments
Keeping the commandments and doing what is right, followed by blessing, possession of the land, and victory over enemies
medium.explanation: The passage first commands obedience and right conduct, then describes the results: well-being, possession of the land, and the defeat of enemies.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by the phrase “Ye shall diligently keep”?
answers: The commandments must be kept with great care
Only some commandments may be kept
The command was given only to Israel’s enemies
challenge.explanation: The wording strongly emphasizes careful and thorough observance of the commandments.

challenge.question: What is the difference between keeping the Lord’s commandments and doing what is right and good?
answers: They are completely unrelated
The first concerns obeying the commands, while the second also emphasizes proper conduct before the Lord
The first is for enemies and the second for kings
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions both obedience to the commandments and morally right conduct pleasing to the Lord.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “as the Lord hath spoken” teach at the end of the passage?
answers: The enemies commanded Israel to act
The promise depends only on Israel’s military strength
The enemies will be driven out according to the Lord’s promise
challenge.explanation: The phrase makes clear that victory over the enemies will occur according to what the Lord has spoken and promised.

questions.question: What is emphasized by the phrase “Ye shall diligently keep”?
answers: The commandments must be kept with great care
Only some commandments may be kept
The command was given only to Israel’s enemies
questions.explanation: The wording strongly emphasizes careful and thorough observance of the commandments.

questions.question: What is the difference between keeping the Lord’s commandments and doing what is right and good?
answers: They are completely unrelated
The first concerns obeying the commands, while the second also emphasizes proper conduct before the Lord
The first is for enemies and the second for kings
questions.explanation: The passage mentions both obedience to the commandments and morally right conduct pleasing to the Lord.

questions.question: What does the phrase “as the Lord hath spoken” teach at the end of the passage?
answers: The enemies commanded Israel to act
The promise depends only on Israel’s military strength
The enemies will be driven out according to the Lord’s promise
questions.explanation: The phrase makes clear that victory over the enemies will occur according to what the Lord has spoken and promised.

paragraphs.title: Telling the Next Generation the Story of the Exodus

easy.question: Who may ask a father about the commandments?
answers: His son
The king of Egypt
His neighbor
easy.explanation: The passage says, “When thy son asketh thee.”

easy.question: Whose bondmen were the Israelites?
answers: Moses’
Pharaoh’s
Their ancestors’
easy.explanation: The Israelites say, “We were Pharaoh’s bondmen in Egypt.”

easy.question: Why did the Lord bring Israel out of Egypt?
answers: So they could return to Egypt
So they could build a palace
So He could bring them into the land
easy.explanation: The Lord brought them out in order to bring them into the land He swore to give their ancestors.

medium.question: What was the order of events according to the passage?
answers: Bondage in Egypt, deliverance, and being brought into the land
Entering the land, becoming enslaved, and then leaving
Leaving Egypt, entering the land, and then becoming enslaved
medium.explanation: Israel was first enslaved, then the Lord brought them out, and finally He brought them into the land.

medium.question: In the question “What mean the testimonies, and the statutes, and the judgments,” what do these terms refer to?
answers: Stories of wars only
Commands and rules that the Lord gave
The names of the Israelites
medium.explanation: The context identifies these terms as the commands and rules given by the Lord.

medium.question: Why does the passage mention the signs and wonders in Egypt?
answers: To explain how the Lord rescued Israel
To teach about Pharaoh’s life
To describe the land only
medium.explanation: The signs and wonders were part of how the Lord brought Israel out of Egyptian bondage.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the father answering, “We were Pharaoh’s bondmen”?
answers: The father is speaking only about himself
The national story is presented as a shared experience of Israel
The son had already lived in Egypt
challenge.explanation: The plural wording connects the father and all Israel with the shared story of slavery and redemption.

challenge.question: What is the connection between the Exodus and receiving the land in verse 23?
answers: The Exodus was a step toward fulfilling the promise of the land
The land was given to Egypt
The Exodus canceled the promise to the ancestors
challenge.explanation: The verse presents the purpose of the Exodus: the Lord brought Israel out in order to bring them into the land promised to the ancestors.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “before our eyes” emphasize in the description of the signs and wonders?
answers: The events happened only in the imagination
The events were secret and unseen
The Israelites experienced them as events they personally witnessed
challenge.explanation: “Before our eyes” emphasizes that the Israelites were direct witnesses of the signs and wonders in Egypt.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the father answering, “We were Pharaoh’s bondmen”?
answers: The father is speaking only about himself
The national story is presented as a shared experience of Israel
The son had already lived in Egypt
questions.explanation: The plural wording connects the father and all Israel with the shared story of slavery and redemption.

questions.question: What is the connection between the Exodus and receiving the land in verse 23?
answers: The Exodus was a step toward fulfilling the promise of the land
The land was given to Egypt
The Exodus canceled the promise to the ancestors
questions.explanation: The verse presents the purpose of the Exodus: the Lord brought Israel out in order to bring them into the land promised to the ancestors.

questions.question: What does the phrase “before our eyes” emphasize in the description of the signs and wonders?
answers: The events happened only in the imagination
The events were secret and unseen
The Israelites experienced them as events they personally witnessed
questions.explanation: “Before our eyes” emphasizes that the Israelites were direct witnesses of the signs and wonders in Egypt.

paragraphs.title: The Commandments for Life and Righteousness

easy.question: What did the Lord command the Israelites to do?
answers: All these statutes
Only one commandment
Build new cities
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord commanded us to do all these statutes.”

easy.question: Why were the Israelites to fear the Lord?
answers: To become famous
So that it might be well with them always
To win wars
easy.explanation: The passage connects fearing the Lord with their good always.

easy.question: What does verse 25 say about keeping the commandments?
answers: They are very difficult
They are intended only for the elders
It will be their righteousness
easy.explanation: The verse says, “It shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments.”

medium.question: What is the connection between keeping the commandments and Israel’s well-being?
answers: Keeping the commandments is intended for their good and their life
Keeping the commandments is intended only to punish them
Keeping the commandments is intended to distance them from the Lord
medium.explanation: The passage says that the commandments were given for Israel’s good always and to preserve them alive.

medium.question: In the phrase “it shall be our righteousness,” what does “righteousness” mean here?
answers: A gift given only to the poor
A right action or standing before the Lord
A punishment for disobedience
medium.explanation: In this context, righteousness refers to doing what is right before the Lord by keeping His commandments.

medium.question: What order of ideas appears in these verses?
answers: Reward, command, and then fear
Life, war, and then commandments
The command to keep the statutes, fear of the Lord, and a good result
medium.explanation: The passage first gives the command, then explains the purpose of fearing the Lord, followed by life and well-being.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the passage mentioning both fear of the Lord and human well-being?
answers: Proper worship includes reverence for the Lord as well as benefit for human life
The commandments are intended only to provide material prosperity
Fear of the Lord removes the need to keep the commandments
challenge.explanation: The passage presents reverence for the Lord together with Israel’s well-being, connecting worship with a good life.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “as he hath commanded us” emphasize?
answers: The commandments may be changed according to personal preference
The commandments must be kept as they were given
Only some commandments are binding
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes obeying the commandments according to the Lord’s instruction rather than changing or selecting them.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “preserve us alive, as it is at this day”?
answers: The commandments were meant only for distant generations
The promised life exists only in the world to come
The commandments are connected with preserving the people’s life in the present
challenge.explanation: The words “as it is at this day” show that the life and blessing connected with the commandments concern the present as well as the future.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the passage mentioning both fear of the Lord and human well-being?
answers: Proper worship includes reverence for the Lord as well as benefit for human life
The commandments are intended only to provide material prosperity
Fear of the Lord removes the need to keep the commandments
questions.explanation: The passage presents reverence for the Lord together with Israel’s well-being, connecting worship with a good life.

questions.question: What does the phrase “as he hath commanded us” emphasize?
answers: The commandments may be changed according to personal preference
The commandments must be kept as they were given
Only some commandments are binding
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes obeying the commandments according to the Lord’s instruction rather than changing or selecting them.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “preserve us alive, as it is at this day”?
answers: The commandments were meant only for distant generations
The promised life exists only in the world to come
The commandments are connected with preserving the people’s life in the present
questions.explanation: The words “as it is at this day” show that the life and blessing connected with the commandments concern the present as well as the future.
